title: Section 87A Tax Rebate Rules
source: Income Tax Department, Government of India (Income Tax Act 1961 & Income Tax Act 2025)
reference: Section 87A, Income Tax Act 1961 — recodified as Section 157 under Income Tax Act 2025
content: Section 87A (recodified as Section 157 under the Income Tax Act 2025) provides a full or partial tax rebate to resident individuals having low or moderate income levels. Under the New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC / Section 202) for Tax Year 2026-27, a resident individual whose taxable income does not exceed ₹12,00,000 is eligible for a Section 87A (Section 157) tax rebate of 100% of income tax payable or ₹60,000, whichever is less. This effectively makes zero tax payable for income up to ₹12.75 lakh (including ₹75k standard deduction) under the New Regime. For example, for an individual with ₹9 lakh income (or 9 lakh annual income), after applying the ₹75,000 standard deduction, the taxable income is ₹8,25,000, which falls below ₹12,00,000; thus the Section 87A rebate of ₹60,000 applies and total tax payable is ₹0. Under the Old Tax Regime, Section 87A rebate is available if taxable income does not exceed ₹5,00,000, with a maximum rebate cap of ₹12,500.
